references.text: Describes the same phenomenon where leaders believed in Jesus but did not confess it publicly for fear of being excluded from the synagogue, just like the parents in John 9.
Jesus' prophecy that those who kill his disciples will think they are doing God's will and will be cast out of the synagogue, which is the direct consequence mentioned in John 9:22.
The first time in the Gospel it is mentioned that no one spoke openly about Jesus for fear of the Jews, a pattern repeated in John 9:22.
Describes Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus as secret disciples who feared the Jews, illustrating the fear of being 'apostsynagotos' which is central to John 9:22.
